items.titleEn: Vlad Jr. expands on comments about his contract, disappointing season
bodyEn: BALTIMORE -- It takes a lot for the Blue Jays’ 2026 elimination to dip below being the story of the day, but that’s exactly what happened Wednesday in Baltimore, as Vladimir Guerrero Jr. addressed some controversial quotes from a recent Spanish-language interview.

In a conversation recently with Veronica Batista, Guerrero addressed his disappointing season and spoke about his 14-year, $500 million extension. Those comments didn’t sit well with fans, though, when Guerrero spoke about being paid for what he’s done for the Blue Jays in the past, not what he’s expected to do in the future.

“I want people to understand one thing,” Guerrero said in Spanish. “The money they gave me wasn’t for what I’m going to do. It was for what I already did. They didn’t pay me because I’m going to hit 40 every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished. People are confused about that, but I think the same way they do. Like, sometimes I even say to myself: bro, they gave you all that money and you’re out here doing nothing. I try.”
Asked about those comments following the Blue Jays being mathematically eliminated from the playoffs Wednesday afternoon, Guerrero stood by them.

"No, I don't regret myself. I'm not lying with what I say,” Guerrero said through interpreter Hector Lebron. “I understand some fans, they don't understand the way and what I was trying to say specifically, but what I said is the way I feel."
This takes us back to the lessons learned in Spring Training of 2025, when Guerrero and the Blue Jays were first negotiating his $500 million extension.

Every few days, another Spanish-language podcast or television appearance featuring Guerrero would be released, often with journalists or interviewers from his native Dominican Republic. It’s important to ensure that nothing is lost in translation, first and foremost, then to contextualize when and why these things were said.
Last spring, for example, a couple of those interviews lingered for weeks at a time before being posted, which stirred up more discourse than anyone -- perhaps even Guerrero -- had planned.

This time, Guerrero’s comments days later seemed to line up with his initial interview with Batista, which was making its rounds on social media throughout Wednesday’s Game 1 of the doubleheader. At one point, Guerrero was also asked to expand on those comments and explain why he was thinking that.

“That was a quote from the interview when she asked me how I felt about this year. I said that, obviously, I feel really bad about the year that I had, that I couldn’t help my team get to the postseason,” Guerrero said. “I said I felt -- that it’s my personal opinion -- that every player gets paid for what they have done. With that said, you guys have got to remember that I signed my contract at the beginning of last year, then I did put up a good year. Then, the kind of playoffs that I had to help the team get into the World Series.”

Getting Guerrero right is the Blue Jays’ No. 1 priority this offseason. It might be No. 2 and No. 3, as well. If he’s hitting 40-plus home runs, then the Blue Jays might have more of an appetite for moments like this, but it lands at a particularly rough time, given the season he’s just had. Guerrero has hit just nine home runs this season with an OPS that’s been hovering below .700.

“He’s got all the potential in the world. We know that. We’ve seen him be one of, if not the best, players in the game,” John Schneider said. “Years like this, they can happen. Myself, the staff and Vlad, he’s not chalking this one up to ‘one of those years.’ He worked tirelessly to get out of the funk he was in. He tried new things. He tried different ways to prepare and he posted every single day. Definitely not what we expected, what he expected. It’s not what we expect out of him going forward and not what he expects out of himself going forward.”
items.titleZh: Vladimir Guerrero Jr.谈合同与失望赛季
items.summaryZh: Vladimir Guerrero Jr.回应了关于其大合同及失望赛季的争议言论。
bodyZh: 巴尔的摩——要让多伦多蓝鸟在2026年的被淘汰出局不再成为头条新闻并不是件容易的事，但在周三的巴尔的摩，情况正是如此，Vladimir Guerrero Jr.就近期一次西班牙语采访中的争议言论做出了解释。
在最近与Veronica Batista的对话中，Guerrero谈到了自己令人失望的赛季以及那份14年5亿美元的续约合同。然而，当Guerrero谈到拿薪水是为了过去为多伦多蓝鸟所做的一切，而非未来预期表现时，这些言论并没有让球迷们感到高兴。
“我希望人们明白一件事，”Guerrero用西班牙语说道，“他们给我的钱不是为了我以后要做什么，而是为了我过去已经做过的事。他们付钱给我不是因为我每年都能打出40个本垒打。他们付钱给我，是因为我已经取得了成就。人们对此感到困惑，但我跟他们的想法是一样的。比如，有时我甚至会对自己说：兄弟，他们给了你那么多钱，而你却在这里无所事事。我一直在努力。”
周三下午多伦多蓝鸟在数学上确定无缘季后赛后，当被问及这些言论时，Guerrero坚持了自己的立场。
“不，我不后悔。我说话没有撒谎，”Guerrero通过翻译Hector Lebron表示，“我理解有些球迷并不理解我当时试图表达的方式和具体内容，但我所说的是我的真实感受。”
这把我们带回了2025年春训期间学到的教训，当时Guerrero和多伦多蓝鸟首次在商讨他5亿美元的续约事宜。
每隔几天，就会有另一档由Guerrero参加的西班牙语播客或电视节目播出，通常采访者来自他的家乡多米尼加共和国。首先，确保翻译不失真至关重要，其次是要弄清楚这些言论发表的时间和背景。
例如，去年春天，其中几项采访在发布前搁置了好几个星期，这引发了比任何人——甚至可能比Guerrero本人——预期中更多的讨论。
这一次，几天后Guerrero的言论似乎与他最初接受Batista采访时一致，该采访在周三的双重赛第一场比赛期间一直在社交媒体上流传。在某个时刻，Guerrero也被要求进一步阐述这些言论，并解释他为什么会有这种想法。
“那是采访中的一句引言，当时她问我如何看待今年。我说，很明显，对于自己度过糟糕的一年、无法帮助球队进入季后赛，我感到非常难过，”Guerrero说，“我说我觉得——这是我个人的看法——每个球员获得薪水都是因为他们过去所做的事。话虽如此，你们必须记住，我是去年初签的合同，后来我确实打出了不错的一年。还有我为了帮助球队进入世界大赛而经历的季后赛。”
让Guerrero找回状态是多伦多蓝鸟今年休赛期的首要任务。这可能也是第二和第三重要的任务。如果他能轰出40多记本垒打，那么多伦多蓝鸟或许对这样的时刻会有更多包容，但在他刚刚经历这样一个赛季之后，时机显得格外艰难。Guerrero本赛季仅打出9支本垒打，OPS一直徘徊在.700以下。

“他拥有无与伦比的潜力。我们都知道这一点。我们见证过他成为比赛中最优秀的球员之一，甚至就是最优秀的球员，”John Schneider说道，“像这样的年份是可能发生的。包括我和教练组在内，以及Vlad在内，他并没有把这归咎于‘碰巧糟糕的一年’。他不知疲倦地工作以走出低谷。他尝试了新事物。他尝试了不同的备战方式，并且每天都出场。这绝对不是我们所期望的，也不是他所期望的。这不是我们对他未来的期望，也不是他对自己的未来所期望的。”

items.titleEn: Scherzer, Blue Jays lament missed opportunities in '26
bodyEn: BALTIMORE -- That’s it, that’s all. The Blue Jays have been eliminated from postseason contention.
You’ve already known that for a few days now, but after Wednesday afternoon’s 4-2 loss to the Orioles in Game 1 of their doubleheader at Camden Yards, the math agrees with it, too.
This is what mattered most:
1. Final American League Wild Card update of 2026

This loss dropped the Blue Jays (77-81) to 4 1/2 games behind the White Sox (81-76) for that third and final spot, and before Game 2 (and the White Sox game tonight), that’s enough to slam the door shut on any microscopic shot at the postseason.

For a team that entered 2026 with World Series expectations, this can only be viewed as a complete and total disappointment. Even in a season with so many challenges -- injuries at the top of that list -- the bar was so low for the Blue Jays to compete for that final AL Wild Card spot. That’s one of the main tragedies of this season, and surely, a Wild Card spot will demand more in 2027 and beyond.

Now, the Wild Card race is all but wrapped up with the Rangers also well back. The Blue Jays and Orioles (77-81), who sit tied after Game 1 of the doubleheader, are now trying to avoid finishing last place in the AL East.
2. Mad Max … Not done yet?

Max Scherzer struck out seven over his five innings of four-run ball on Wednesday, leaving him with 3,550, the ninth most in MLB history. This puts him four strikeouts shy of Justin Verlander (3,554) for eighth all-time.

Verlander is scheduled to pitch on Saturday for the Tigers, his grand finale at Comerica Park before retirement, and he could extend that lead by a few more. That leaves the Blue Jays with an interesting decision to make, as Scherzer would be on short rest to pitch in the final game of the season.

“There’s a chance he comes back on Sunday. That’s what the initial plan was,” manager John Schneider said pregame. “I know it’s a day shorter, but we’ll see how today goes and figure that out in the next couple of days. We kind of wanted to get him one more.”
So, will Scherzer or the Blue Jays be watching that strikeout race on Saturday before making their call about Sunday? Schneider thought for a moment and laughed.
“He may.”
3. Scherzer’s impact on the Blue Jays

Scherzer’s two seasons with the Blue Jays have been defined by injuries, the likely future Hall of Famer constantly fighting back against his thumb, his back, his forearm, his ankle and his age. The numbers don’t tell a kind story, but Scherzer’s impact on the organization stretches well beyond that.

He’s spent nearly as much time in Schneider’s office as he has. One day, it might be an hour-long conversation about a single pitch. The next day, it’s 45 minutes of Scherzer breaking down the positioning of his outfielders. Schneider will never experience another player like this again.

“I love having him. Does it get exhausting sometimes? Yeah,” Schneider said, laughing. “I think there’s a certain edge that he brings, too. Not just on games that he starts, but having that presence through the day to day of a baseball season is really cool. He’s helped me exponentially. He’s taught me things. He’s not afraid to come in and check my work.”

If this is the end of the line for Scherzer, it’s been one of the greatest pitching careers we’ve ever seen. The Blue Jays didn’t see his best days on the mound, but they’re still a better organization for having him wear their uniform.
items.titleZh: Scherzer与蓝鸟遗憾无缘2026年季后赛
items.summaryZh: 蓝鸟在双重赛首战输给金莺后正式无缘2026年季后赛。
bodyZh: 巴尔的摩讯——就是这样，全部结束了。多伦多蓝鸟已经无缘季后赛。
其实大家几天前就已经知道了，但在周三下午于金莺球场举行的双重赛首战以2-4输给巴尔的摩金莺之后，数学上的可能也彻底宣告破灭。
以下是几个关键要点：
1. 2026年美国联盟外卡争夺最终更新
这场失利让蓝鸟（77胜81负）在争夺美联第三张也是最后一张外卡席位上落后芝加哥白袜（81胜76负）4场半胜场差。在第二场比赛（以及今晚白袜的比赛）开始前，这已经彻底关上了晋级季后赛的微小希望之门。
对于一支带着争夺世界大赛期望进入2026赛季的球队来说，这只能被视为一次彻底的失望。即便在一个充满挑战的赛季中——伤病高居榜首——蓝鸟只需达到很低的门槛就能竞争美联最后一张外卡席位。这是本赛季的主要悲剧之一，可以肯定的是，2027年及以后对外卡席位的争夺将会更加激烈。
如今，随着得克萨斯游骑兵同样落后较多，外卡争夺战基本尘埃落定。双重赛首战打完后战绩同为77胜81负的蓝鸟和巴尔的摩金莺，现在正努力避免在美国联盟东区垫底。
2. 传奇老将Max Scherzer……还没结束？
Max Scherzer在周三投满了5局丢4分并送出7次三振，这使他的生涯三振总数达到3,550次，在MLB历史排行榜上位列第九。这让他距离排在历史第八位的Justin Verlander（3,554次）仅差4次三振。
Justin Verlander预计将在周六为底特律老虎先发登板，这将是他在科莫卡公园球场的退役前告别演出，他可能会将这一领先优势进一步扩大。这也让蓝鸟面临一个有趣的决定，因为Scherzer如果要在赛季最后一场比赛中登板，将需要缩短休息天数。
“他周日有可能会回归。这原本是最初的计划，”总教练John Schneider在赛前表示，“我知道休息天数少了一天，但我们要看今天的情况如何，并在接下来的一天左右弄清楚。我们本来就想让他再投一场。”
那么，Scherzer或蓝鸟会在周六观看那场三振数追逐战，然后再决定周日的安排吗？Schneider思索了一下，笑了笑。
“他可能会的。”
3. Scherzer对蓝鸟的影响
Scherzer在蓝鸟效力的两个赛季饱受伤病困扰，这位未来大概率入选名人堂的投手一直在跟自己的拇指、背部、前臂、脚踝以及年龄做斗争。数据并不算好看，但Scherzer对这支球队的影响远超于此。
他在Schneider办公室里待的时间几乎和在场上差不多。有时，他们会针对单一投球进行长达一个小时的讨论；有时，则是Scherzer花45分钟剖析外野手的站位。Schneider再也不会遇到像他这样的球员了。
“我很喜欢拥有他。有时会觉得精疲力竭吗？是的，”Schneider笑着说，“我认为他也带来了一种特质。不仅在他先发登板的日子里，在漫长棒球赛季的每一天里都有这种存在感，这真的很酷。他对我帮助极大。他教了我很多东西。他甚至敢于走进来检查我的工作。”
如果这是Scherzer职业生涯的终点，那这也是我们见过的最伟大的投球生涯之一。蓝鸟虽然没有见证他在投手丘上的巅峰岁月，但因为他身披这件球衣，这支球队变得更好了。
